description: I'm interested in space technology, AI, software development, and solving real-world environmental problems. I'm planning to work on an Earth System Trend Detection platform using NASA datasets to analyse changes in temperature, rainfall, and other environmental indicators. I'm looking for enthusiastic team members interested in Python, web development, data analysis, UI/UX design, and creative problem-solving. Let's build something meaningful together!
summary: TERRADETECH (Earth Trend Detective) turns NASA's open Earth-observation data into a narrated story of environmental change. A user picks any place and a range of years. A 3D Earth built from NASA Blue Marble imagery spins, flies to that location and travels back in time through real NASA GIBS satellite imagery, while an AI voice-over with live captions explains what changed. The numbers come from NASA POWER climate data, MODIS vegetation and land-surface temperature, and GPM IMERG rainfall, compared with a 1991-2020 baseline to flag unusual months with a confidence value. A trained Isolation Forest model gives a second opinion. The platform has four connected features: AI anomaly detection, multi-satellite comparison (MODIS beside Landsat/Sentinel-2 HLS), an animated environmental timeline, and Earth Story Mode. It addresses the challenge "[name of your challenge]" by making complex NASA data understandable for students, communities and planners. The narration is written only from calculated results, so no statistics are invented.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

TERRADETECH lets anyone explore how a place on Earth has changed using real NASA data. The user enters a place and a period of years and presses play. Earth rotates in 3D, the camera flies to the location, the year counter runs back to the start year, and real NASA satellite imagery fades in year by year. An AI voice-over with live captions explains the real calculated results, ending with a final report card.

FOUR CONNECTED FEATURES

A. AI Anomaly Detection: monthly air temperature, precipitation, root-zone soil wetness, MODIS NDVI, MODIS land-surface temperature and GPM IMERG rainfall are compared against a 1991-2020 baseline using z-scores. Unusual months are listed with value, baseline, date and a confidence value. A trained Isolation Forest model adds a second opinion.

B. Multi-Satellite Comparison: four linked maps show MODIS Terra, MODIS Aqua, HLS Sentinel-2 and HLS Landsat for the same place and date, with native resolution (250 m vs 30 m) and real acquisition dates from NASA CMR.

F. Animated Timeline: a narrated time-lapse of real NASA imagery with a live temperature chart and anomaly markers.

G. Earth Story Mode: the cinematic journey from orbit to the chosen place, with voice-over, captions and a final environmental report.

HOW IT WORKS

A Python FastAPI backend downloads NASA data, caches it, calculates baselines, anomalies and trends, and builds the narration only from the calculated numbers. A React and Three.js frontend shows the 3D Earth (NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble textures), maps, charts and the cinematic player. If a NASA source is unavailable, the app shows a clear message instead of any substitute data.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, React, Vite, Three.js, Leaflet, Recharts, browser Web Speech API for the voice-over, Render and Vercel for hosting.

IMPACT

It helps students, communities and planners see unusual environmental change quickly and understand it without expert tools.

CREATIVITY

Instead of showing only graphs, the platform turns data into a cinematic story that travels through time from a global view to a chosen place.

LIMITATIONS

Climate values come from NASA POWER at roughly half-degree resolution. MODIS values are for a single pixel at the chosen point and can have gaps from cloud or water. Soil wetness is a POWER model value, not SMAP. Anomaly flags are statistical indicators, not proof of cause. Planned next: SMAP soil moisture and pixel-level HLS vegetation change.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE

The code, documentation text and demo slide text were developed with help from Claude (Anthropic), an AI assistant. The team reviewed, ran, tested and integrated the output. The voice-over uses the browser's built-in speech synthesis. No SI-generated images or video are used, and no NASA logos or branding are used. All imagery comes from NASA services.
